Your name probably cannot be a Nostr petname any more.

On 20 September 2026 at 16:53 UTC, commit 46f8e95 added one sentence to NIP-02: a petname qualifies for resolution only if it contains ASCII letters, numbers or the underscore. One file, one line added, pushed straight to master with no pull request. That excludes spaces, the slash, the hyphen, the period, accented Latin characters, and every non-Latin script: Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, CJK.

PR #2472 had merged petname paths like ~/erin/charlie the day before and left escaping undefined. This does not define escaping. It deletes the characters that would have needed it.

We read every commit that lands on nostr-protocol/nips, not just the merged pull requests, which is the only reason this one surfaced at all. Does the petname in your kind 3 follow list still qualify?

The honest limit: the sentence never names its subject, it uses a lowercase must where NIP-02 uses SHOULD elsewhere, and no client release yet cites the rule. Storing an ineligible petname is still unvalidated by anything in the spec.
